Summarize a Hammel model

Source: R/hammel_model.R
summary.hammel_model.Rd

Summary method for class "hammel_model"

Usage

# S3 method for class 'hammel_model'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.hammel_model'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A hammel_model object returned by hammel_model().

...

Additional arguments passed to summary.hammel_population().

x

A summary.hammel_model object returned by summary.hammel_model().

Value

summary() returns an object of class summary.hammel_model containing:

population

The summary.hammel_population of the starting population, or NULL when no population is set.

groups

A named list with one element per group dimension, or NULL when the model has none. Each element contains group (the summary.hammel_group of the declared dimension, reporting the population's categories when a population is set, or NULL when the dimension is not declared) and transition (the summary.hammel_group_transition of the dimension's transition process, or NULL when it has none).

processes

A named list of process summaries, in the order mortality, fertility, union formation, union dissolution, for the processes present.

missing

A character vector naming the required elements that are not set: any of "population", "mortality", "fertility", and "union_formation", plus "transition:<dimension>" for each group transition process whose dimension is not declared ("transition:.default" for a process without group when the model does not declare exactly one dimension). Empty when the model has the elements needed to run a simulation.

print() displays each component summary in turn, followed by whether the model has the elements needed to run a simulation and, if not, which are missing. It returns its input invisibly.

Details

The summary combines the summaries of the starting population, of each group dimension and its transition process, and of each other process in the model, and records which elements required by run_simulation() are missing.

See also

hammel_model(), run_simulation()

Examples

model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(generate_uniform_population(1000)) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility)
summary(model)
